html:
The Nyangumarta are an Aboriginal people of the northwest coast of Western Australia, along Eighty Mile Beach and inland into the Great Sandy Desert, between the Pilbara and Broome. The anthropologist Norman Tindale described two branches: the Kundal on the coast and the Iparuka inland.

Their country joins the sea with the desert. Coastal people fished and gathered shellfish, while inland groups lived from seeds, game and waterholes. Neighbours were the Karajarri to the north, the Ngarla and Nyamal to the southwest, and desert peoples such as the Mangala to the east.

From the 1860s pastoral stations and the pearling industry spread along this coast, and many Aboriginal people were forced into work. The Nyangumarta language is still spoken today, unlike many of its neighbours. Their wider story is told in Aboriginal Australian societies.
